explanation: Build one lowercase token while scanning letters and punctuation whose immediate neighbors are letters. On any separator, increment the completed token’s dictionary count and clear it. A final sentinel separator flushes a token ending at the last input character.
correctness: Each maximal sequence satisfying the disclosed token grammar is emitted once. Lowercasing maps permitted case variants to the same dictionary key, and one increment per token gives its occurrence count.
walkthrough: For "Owls fly; OWLS don't crawl. Fly-by owls!", punctuation ends tokens but internal apostrophes and letter-surrounded hyphens remain. Lowercasing combines Owls, OWLS and owls into count 3. The other keys are fly, don't, crawl and fly-by, each counted once under the disclosed bank policy. Construct WordCloudData from the input string and inspect WordsToCounts; the displayed dictionary is the exposed property, not a constructor return value. Dictionary order is irrelevant.
edgeCases: Empty text yields an empty dictionary. red--blue splits into red and blue; a letter-surrounded apostrophe or single hyphen remains inside a token.
timeComplexity: Expected O(n) time: tokenization, lowercase conversion and hashing examine O(n) total characters. The dictionary performs one expected constant-time update per token after hashing.
spaceComplexity: O(n) worst-case storage for dictionary keys and current token; an implementation that materializes all matches also stores O(n) matched characters.
